narration.en: Euclid found the GCD by recursion 2300 years ago. Fibonacci numbers, binary search, reversing a string and converting to binary all have short recursive solutions.

body.en: Many number problems reduce to a smaller one. GCD (Euclid): gcd(a, b) = a if b == 0, else gcd(b, a % b). Power: pow(x, n) = 1 if n == 0, else x * pow(x, n − 1). Sum of digits: sod(n) = 0 if n == 0, else n % 10 + sod(n / 10). Fibonacci: fib(n) = n if n <= 1, else fib(n − 1) + fib(n − 2). Decimal to binary: bin(n) prints bin(n / 2) and then n % 2.

points.en: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b); gcd(a, 0) = a

body.en: Recursion also works on strings and arrays by shrinking an index range. Reverse a string: rev(s) = "" if s is empty, else rev(s.substring(1)) + s.charAt(0). Palindrome: check the first and last characters and recurse on the middle. Binary search: search(a, key, low, high) returns −1 if low > high; otherwise compares a[mid] and recurses on one half. Sum of an array: sum(a, i) = 0 if i == a.length, else a[i] + sum(a, i + 1).
